properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: Pure-JS SHA-1/SHA-2 (and RIPEMD-160) implementation, a transitive dependency of elliptic inside the web3 stack (crypto-browserify shim). No direct call site in the app's own sources; it ships with the bundle web3 pulls in. Same logical asset as the hash.js@1.1.7 dependency object — linked same_as so the reader needs one entry.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: Native JS bindings for ECDSA over secp256k1, pulled in by web3@1.5.1 → web3-eth-accounts → ethereumjs-util@7 (elliptic is its pure-JS fallback). The app's live use is the mint flow: every transaction is a secp256k1 ECDSA signature delegated to the user's MetaMask wallet. Changeable here only by upgrading web3/the chain ecosystem; the signing curve is fixed by the Ethereum protocol, observable from this repo. Same tree is also declared in yarn.lock.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: OpenSSL EVP_BytesToKey single-round MD5-based KDF polyfill, shipped in the production browser bundle via web3-eth-accounts → crypto-browserify (web3's Node-crypto shim). Weak-KDF practice but used for cipher-key derivation in the shim, not for user passwords. Changeable here by dependency upgrade. The same shim also ships md5.js@1.3.5 (entry 10668), ripemd160@2.0.2 (entry 14022) and create-hmac@1.1.6 (entry 4842) via create-hash@1.2.0 (entry 4830) — none of which the collectors recorded.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: Not bcrypt password hashing for app users: bcrypt-pbkdf is the bcrypt-based PBKDF (OpenBSD bcrypt_pbkdf) used by sshpk only to parse/serialize OpenSSH-format private keys. It rides the web3-bzz → swarm-js → servify → request → http-signature → sshpk chain and is browser-bundled with web3; no first-party call site.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: node-forge's RSA serves only the react-scripts dev server (self-signed HTTPS cert generation) — not shipped in the production bundle. The RSA that DOES ship to browsers is public-encrypt@4.0.3 (RSAES-PKCS1-v1_5, entry 13041, required by crypto-browserify at 4887) and browserify-rsa@4.1.0 (RSA PKCS#1 sign/verify, entry 4026) under browserify-sign@4.2.1 (4035) — all via web3-eth-accounts → crypto-browserify. Both halves are harvestable/breakable under Shor; migrate encryption to ML-KEM-768 and sig

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: Elliptic-curve Diffie-Hellman polyfill shipped in the production bundle: web3-eth-accounts@1.5.3 → crypto-browserify@3.12.0 → create-ecdh (over elliptic, typically secp256k1 in the Ethereum stack). Retroactively breakable under Shor — harvest-now-decrypt-later if any peer traffic uses it; the app itself calls no crypto directly. The same crypto-browserify requires block also ships finite-field diffie-hellman@5.0.3 (entry 5487, required at 4884), which the collectors did not record. Changeable he

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: tweetnacl@0.14.5's Ed25519 (nacl.sign) capability, shipped in the production bundle via web3-bzz → swarm-js → servify → request → http-signature → sshpk → bcrypt-pbkdf → tweetnacl (entry package-lock.json:15852). No first-party call site — the app performs no crypto directly. Quantum-relevant: Ed25519 signatures break under Shor; migration ML-DSA-65 at the library level (changeable via dependency upgrade).

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: elliptic@6.5.4 is web3's pure-JS ECDSA (secp256k1 and other curves, plus ECDH) library, required by ethereumjs-util/secp256k1 in the web3-eth-accounts chain. Shipped with the app's dependency tree; also declared in yarn.lock. Same logical asset as the elliptic@6.5.4 dependency object — linked same_as.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: tweetnacl@0.14.5's X25519 (nacl.box / nacl.scalarMult) capability in the same production chain (web3-bzz → ... → sshpk → bcrypt-pbkdf → tweetnacl). Shor-vulnerable key agreement if ever exercised; no first-party call site. Migration ML-KEM-768.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: Keccak-256 is Ethereum's workhorse hash (transaction hashes, address derivation, ABI function-signature selectors). Declared in both package-lock.json and yarn.lock; no direct call in the app's own sources — web3 invokes it when encoding the mint() call and computing receipt hashes. Keccak-256 is quantum-safe in the symmetric sense (Grover only); kept as dependency inventory.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: pbkdf2@3.1.2 is required by crypto-browserify inside web3-eth-accounts; web3's V3 keystore (secret-storage) key derivation uses pbkdf2 (or scrypt) when importing an encrypted wallet file. Dependency inventory — no direct call in the app's own sources. Also declared in yarn.lock. Same logical asset as the pbkdf2@3.1.2 dependency object.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: scrypt-js is the Ethereum Secret Storage (keystore v3) KDF, in the production bundle on two chains: web3-eth-accounts@1.5.3 requires scrypt-js ^3.0.1 directly (package-lock.json:16696) and via ethereumjs-util → ethereum-cryptography@0.1.3 (requires scrypt-js ^3.0.0, line 6667). Password KDF — memory-hard, quantum-resistant in practice; parameters set at call time. Changeable here by dependency upgrade.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: node-forge's AES serves only the react-scripts dev server (self-signed HTTPS cert path). Separately and more importantly, the AES that ships to browsers is browserify-aes@1.2.0 (CBC/CFB/CTR/GCM) via web3-eth-accounts → crypto-browserify → browserify-cipher AND web3-eth-accounts → ethereumjs-util → ethereum-cryptography — reported this session as its own finding pinned at yarn.lock:3216 (the package-lock.json lines were covered by this object's whole-file location). Changeable here by dependency

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: tweetnacl@0.14.5's authenticated encryption (nacl.secretbox/nacl.box = XSalsa20-Poly1305) in the same production chain as the Ed25519/X25519 capabilities (web3-bzz → ... → sshpk → bcrypt-pbkdf → tweetnacl). Symmetric AE — Grover halves the 256-bit key to 128-bit quantum, still adequate; no first-party call site. Changeable by dependency upgrade.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: Pure-JS NaCl crypto library (Ed25519 sign, X25519 key agreement, XSalsa20-Poly1305 AE) riding the web3-bzz → swarm-js → servify → request → http-signature → sshpk → bcrypt-pbkdf → tweetnacl chain, so it ships in the production bundle despite being seven levels transitive. Its capabilities are recorded as the separate Ed25519/X25519/XSalsa20-Poly1305 objects. properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: node-forge is the crypto provider behind the react-scripts 4.0.3 dev server's self-signed HTTPS certificate (required by selfsigned@1.10.11: yarn.lock:10725 `node-forge "^0.10.0"`). Dev tooling only — not shipped in the production bundle. Its capabilities are recorded as the separate RSA/X.509/AES objects. The "." site is the same declaration seen by the dep scanner; both lockfiles confirm it (package-lock.json, yarn.lock:8339-8341). Changeable here via react-scripts upgrade.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: selfsigned generates the self-signed dev HTTPS certificate for react-scripts 4.0.3's webpack-dev-server (required at package-lock.json:17187, yarn.lock:10720-10725), minting an RSA-2048 self-signed X.509 cert via node-forge when the dev server runs with HTTPS=true. Dev-only, observable here, replaceable only by upgrading react-scripts/webpack-dev-server — never shipped to production visitors.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: node-forge's X.509 machinery (cert creation/parsing/verification) behind the same dev-server chain: react-scripts 4.0.3 → webpack-dev-server → selfsigned@1.10.11 → node-forge@0.10.0. Observable here; the algorithm set is fixed by the vendored library version until react-scripts is upgraded. Not shipped in the production bundle.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: scrypt-js@3.0.1 is web3-eth-accounts' scrypt KDF for Ethereum V3 keystore files (secret-storage: scrypt N=8192/r=8/p=1, or PBKDF2). Shipped in the dependency tree; the app itself never imports a keystore — the wallet holds the keys. Same logical asset as the scrypt algorithm object (its example sites are scrypt-js entries). Also declared in yarn.lock.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: sha.js is the pure-JS SHA-1/SHA-2 stream implementation used by pbkdf2/browserify-cipher inside web3's crypto-browserify shim; the shipped bundle carries it even though the app's own sources never hash anything. Dependency inventory; also in yarn.lock.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: elliptic@6.5.4 gives web3's account layer its pure-JS ECDSA/secp256k1 (and ECDH); it is the live signing library behind web3-eth-accounts when no native binding is present. The app's mint transactions ride on it via the wallet path. Also declared in yarn.lock.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: selfsigned is a dev-time dependency of react-scripts 4.0.3 (CRA) → webpack-dev-server: it generates the throwaway self-signed RSA cert for local HTTPS if the dev server is started with HTTPS. Dev infrastructure only — never used by the app's runtime code or the production bundle; kept because the lockfile ships it. Its X.509/RSA siblings are covered by the node-forge and X.509 objects.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: hash.js provides elliptic's hashing (SHA-1/SHA-2/RIPEMD160) inside the web3 stack; no direct app call site, but the shipped tree carries it. Also declared in yarn.lock. Same logical asset as the "SHA family via hash.js@1.1.7" algorithm object.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: pbkdf2@3.1.2 is the browser PBKDF2 implementation web3-eth-accounts uses for V3 keystore key derivation (and crypto-browserify generally). No direct app call site; ships with the bundle. Also declared in yarn.lock. Same logical asset as the PBKDF2 algorithm object.
